newsitem.title: USA: Stronger U.S. voice needed on farm subsidies-Lugar.
newsitem.headline: Stronger U.S. voice needed on farm subsidies-Lugar.

text.p: The Clinton administration needs to speak far more forcefully if it wants to deter the Europen Union from using grain export subsidies, U.S. Sen. Richard Lugar, R-Ind, said Thursday.
Lugar, chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee, said the administration should act "much more strongly. If they did so, it (resumption of subsidized sales) would not happen."
For more than a year, neither the EU nor the U.S. has employed export subsidies. With a large grain harvest in sight, France is pressing for resumption of sizable subsidies.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman has warned the United States would retaliate if the EU adopts a broad-scale export subsidy plan.
Lugar, however, said a wider range of pressure was needed. He contended the EU was trying to gauge U.S. intent and would respond to a show of resolve.
Glickman has not responded to a letter from Lugar which argues against any use of U.S. export subsidies.
During a speech to a grain trade conference, Lugar said his committee would begin work early next year on reauthorization of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
